## Data Acquisition


```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(tidycensus)
library(sf)
library(httr2)
library(fs)
library(gt)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp03")
fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse = TRUE)

# Nepalese in table B02018 (Asian alone or in any combination, by group).
# Checked for 2024 ACS-1 and ACS-5: B02018_024 = "South Asian: Nepalese".
# NOTE: this number changed between years (it was B02018_016 in 2021),
# so re-check it if you switch to a different year.
GROUP_VAR <- "B02018_024"
ACS_YEAR  <- 2024
```

```{r}
#| label: acs-cache-helper
# Same caching idea as MP02: only hit the API if the file isn't saved yet.
# To refresh (e.g. after adding variables), delete the matching .rds file.
get_acs_cached <- function(file_name, ...){
    file_path <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, paste0(file_name, ".rds"))

    if(!fs::file_exists(file_path)){
        result <- get_acs(...)
        saveRDS(result, file_path)
    }

    readRDS(file_path)
}
```

### Metro Area (CBSA) Population

```{r}
#| label: task1-cbsa
# Task 1: total population and Nepalese population for every metro area (ACS-5; ACS-1 suppresses Nepalese counts)
cbsa_pop <- get_acs_cached(
    "cbsa_nepalese_acs5",
    geography = "cbsa",
    variables = c(total = "B01003_001", nepalese = GROUP_VAR),
    year      = ACS_YEAR,
    survey    = "acs5",
    output    = "wide"
) |>
    mutate(nepalese_share = nepaleseE / totalE)

# Full B02018 table for every metro, used for the ancestry-mix question (Q5)
cbsa_asian_groups <- get_acs_cached(
    "cbsa_b02018_acs5",
    geography = "cbsa",
    table     = "B02018",
    year      = ACS_YEAR,
    survey    = "acs5"
)

# Variable labels, so B02018_0xx codes can be turned into group names
acs1_vars <- {
    f <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "acs5_variables.rds")
    if(!fs::file_exists(f)) saveRDS(load_variables(ACS_YEAR, "acs5"), f)
    readRDS(f)
}

# National total, used for the "share of all US Nepalese" question (Q6)
us_pop <- get_acs_cached(
    "us_nepalese_acs5",
    geography = "us",
    variables = c(total = "B01003_001", nepalese = GROUP_VAR),
    year      = ACS_YEAR,
    survey    = "acs5",
    output    = "wide"
)
```

### NYC Neighborhood Tabulation Areas

```{r}
#| label: task3-nta
# Task 3: download, unzip and read the 2020 NTA shapefile (not via tidycensus)
load_nyc_nta <- function(){
    NTA_URL  <- "https://s-media.nyc.gov/agencies/dcp/assets/files/zip/data-tools/bytes/neighborhood-tabulation-areas/nynta2020_26c.zip"
    zip_file <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "nynta2020.zip")

    if(!fs::file_exists(zip_file)){
        request(NTA_URL) |>
            req_headers(
                `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
            ) |>
            req_retry(max_tries = 4) |>
            req_perform(path = zip_file)
    }

    # Stop early if the download isn't a real zip (e.g. a web page)
    # (every real zip file starts with the letters "PK")
    zip_ok <- identical(readBin(zip_file, "raw", 2), charToRaw("PK"))
    if(!zip_ok){
        fs::file_delete(zip_file)
        stop("NTA download is not a valid zip file. Check NTA_URL.")
    }

    shp_file <- fs::dir_ls(DATA_DIR, recurse = TRUE, glob = "*nynta2020*.shp")

    if(length(shp_file) == 0){
        unzip(zip_file, exdir = DATA_DIR, unzip = "unzip")  # macOS system unzip
        shp_file <- fs::dir_ls(DATA_DIR, recurse = TRUE, glob = "*nynta2020*.shp")
    }

    st_read(shp_file[1], quiet = TRUE) |>
        # NTAType: 0 = residential neighborhood; other codes are parks,
        # airports, cemeteries etc. Kept so those can be filtered out later.
        select(BoroName, NTA2020, NTAName, NTAType)
}

nyc_nta <- load_nyc_nta()
```

### Aggregating Tracts to Neighborhoods

```{r}
#| label: task4-tract-to-nta
# Task 4: give each tract the NTA it overlaps most, then add tracts up per NTA.
# 2020 NTAs are built from whole 2020 tracts, so largest = TRUE is a clean match.
nyc_tracts <- st_transform(nyc_tracts, st_crs(nyc_nta))

tract_to_nta <- nyc_tracts |>
    st_join(nyc_nta, join = st_intersects, largest = TRUE)

nta_pop <- tract_to_nta |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    group_by(NTA2020) |>
    summarize(
        total    = sum(totalE, na.rm = TRUE),
        nepalese = sum(nepaleseE, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups  = "drop"
    )

nta_data <- nyc_nta |>
    left_join(nta_pop, by = "NTA2020") |>
    mutate(nepalese_share = nepalese / total)
```

### NYC PLUTO (Tax Lot Data)

```{r}
#| label: task5-pluto
# Task 5: page through the PLUTO API and save one CSV (cached like MP02)
load_pluto <- function(){
    PLUTO_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "pluto.csv")

    if(!fs::file_exists(PLUTO_FILE)){
        BASE_URL  <- "https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/64uk-42ks.csv"
        # Only the columns needed later
        PLUTO_COLS <- c("bbl", "borough", "bct2020", "landuse",
                        "lotarea", "bldgarea", "comarea", "resarea",
                        "officearea", "retailarea",
                        "unitsres", "unitstotal", "numfloors")
        PAGE_SIZE <- 50000
        offset    <- 0
        pages     <- list()

        repeat {
            page <- request(BASE_URL) |>
                req_url_query(
                    `$select` = paste(PLUTO_COLS, collapse = ","),
                    `$order`  = "bbl",          # fixed order so pages don't overlap
                    `$limit`  = PAGE_SIZE,
                    `$offset` = offset
                ) |>
                req_retry(max_tries = 4) |>
                req_perform() |>
                resp_body_string() |>
                read_csv(col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))

            if(nrow(page) == 0) break
            pages[[length(pages) + 1]] <- page
            if(nrow(page) < PAGE_SIZE) break
            offset <- offset + PAGE_SIZE
        }

        bind_rows(pages) |> write_csv(PLUTO_FILE)
    }

    read_csv(
        PLUTO_FILE,
        col_types = cols(
            bbl = col_character(), borough = col_character(),
            bct2020 = col_character(), landuse = col_character(),
            .default = col_double()
        )
    )
}

pluto <- load_pluto()

# bct2020 = borough digit + 6-digit tract (e.g. 1000100).
# Convert to the Census GEOID (e.g. 36061000100) so PLUTO can join to tracts.
BORO_TO_COUNTY <- c("1" = "061", "2" = "005", "3" = "047", "4" = "081", "5" = "085")

pluto <- pluto |>
    mutate(
        bct2020 = str_remove(bct2020, "\\.0+$"),
        GEOID   = paste0("36",
                         BORO_TO_COUNTY[str_sub(bct2020, 1, 1)],
                         str_sub(bct2020, 2))
    )

# One row per tract with building totals, for the EDA questions
tract_buildings <- pluto |>
    filter(!is.na(bct2020)) |>
    group_by(GEOID) |>
    summarize(
        office_area = sum(officearea, na.rm = TRUE),
        res_area    = sum(resarea,    na.rm = TRUE),
        com_area    = sum(comarea,    na.rm = TRUE),
        bldg_area   = sum(bldgarea,   na.rm = TRUE),
        res_units   = sum(unitsres,   na.rm = TRUE),
        max_floors  = if (all(is.na(numfloors))) NA_real_ else max(numfloors, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups     = "drop"
    )
```

```{r}
#| label: data-check
# Quick sanity checks: run these and look at the numbers before moving on
tibble(
    check = c("Metros", "NYC tracts", "NTAs", "PLUTO lots",
              "PLUTO tracts matched to Census tracts"),
    value = c(nrow(cbsa_pop), nrow(nyc_tracts), nrow(nyc_nta), nrow(pluto),
              sum(tract_buildings$GEOID %in% nyc_tracts$GEOID))
) |>
    gt()
```

## Exploratory Data Analysis

```{r}
#| label: eda-prep
library(scales)

# One row per NYC tract: Census population + its NTA + PLUTO building totals
tract_lookup <- tract_to_nta |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    select(GEOID, tract_name = NAME, NTA2020, NTAName, BoroName,
           pop = totalE, nepalese = nepaleseE)

tract_full <- tract_lookup |>
    left_join(tract_buildings, by = "GEOID")
```


### Q3. Most Crowded Tracts

```{r}
#| label: tbl-q3-density
# Small denominators give silly results (e.g. a tract with 2 apartments and
# a big dorm or prison), so only tracts with a real amount of housing count.
q3 <- tract_full |>
    filter(pop >= 500, res_area >= 50000, res_units >= 50) |>
    mutate(
        pop_per_1000_sqft = pop / res_area * 1000,
        pop_per_unit      = pop / res_units
    )

q3_sqft <- q3 |> slice_max(pop_per_1000_sqft, n = 5) |>
    mutate(measure = "People per 1,000 sq ft of residential space")
q3_unit <- q3 |> slice_max(pop_per_unit, n = 5) |>
    mutate(measure = "People per residential unit")

same_top_tract <- q3_sqft$GEOID[1] == q3_unit$GEOID[1]

bind_rows(q3_sqft, q3_unit) |>
    select(measure, tract_name, NTAName, pop, pop_per_1000_sqft, pop_per_unit) |>
    gt(groupname_col = "measure") |>
    cols_label(tract_name = "Census Tract", NTAName = "Neighborhood",
               pop = "Population", pop_per_1000_sqft = "per 1,000 sq ft",
               pop_per_unit = "per unit") |>
    fmt_number(pop, decimals = 0) |>
    fmt_number(c(pop_per_1000_sqft, pop_per_unit), decimals = 2) |>
    tab_header(title = "Most Densely Housed NYC Tracts, Two Ways")
```

### Q5. Asian Ancestry Mix in Another Large Metro

```{r}
#| label: fig-q5-ancestry
# Default: the non-NYC metro with the most Nepalese residents.
# You can replace this with any metro name from cbsa_pop$NAME.
COMPARISON_METRO <- cbsa_pop |>
    filter(!str_detect(NAME, "New York-Newark"), !is.na(nepaleseE)) |>
    slice_max(nepaleseE, n = 1) |>
    pull(NAME)

# Turn labels like "Estimate!!Total Groups Tallied:!!South Asian:!!Nepalese"
# into a broad region ("South Asian") and keep only the bottom-level rows,
# so nothing is counted twice.
b02018_labels <- acs1_vars |>
    filter(str_starts(name, "B02018_")) |>
    transmute(
        variable = name,
        depth    = str_count(label, "!!"),
        region   = str_remove(str_split_i(label, "!!", 3), ":$"),
        is_header = str_ends(label, ":")
    ) |>
    filter(depth >= 2, !is_header)

q5 <- cbsa_asian_groups |>
    filter(NAME == COMPARISON_METRO) |>
    inner_join(b02018_labels, by = "variable") |>
    group_by(region) |>
    summarize(people = sum(estimate, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(q5, aes(x = people, y = fct_reorder(region, people))) +
    geom_col(fill = "#2a7f8f") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = comma) +
    labs(
        title    = paste("Asian Ancestry Groups in", COMPARISON_METRO),
        subtitle = "ACS 2024 5-year; people reporting more than one group are counted in each",
        x = "People", y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
```

### Q7. Population vs. Housing

```{r}
#| label: fig-q7-pop-housing
q7 <- tract_full |> filter(pop > 0, res_units > 0)
pop_unit_cor <- cor(q7$pop, q7$res_units)

ggplot(q7, aes(x = res_units, y = pop)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 0.8) +
    geom_smooth(aes(color = "Straight line"), method = "lm", se = FALSE) +

    scale_x_continuous(labels = comma) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Straight line" = "#d1495b",
                                  "Flexible curve" = "#2a7f8f")) +
    labs(title = "Population vs. Residential Units, NYC Census Tracts",
         x = "Residential units (PLUTO)", y = "Population (ACS 2024 5-year)",
         color = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
```

### Q8. Neighborhoods with the Tallest Buildings

```{r}
#| label: tbl-q8-floors
q8 <- pluto |>
    filter(!is.na(numfloors), numfloors > 0) |>
    inner_join(tract_lookup |> select(GEOID, NTA2020, NTAName, BoroName),
               by = "GEOID") |>
    group_by(NTA2020, NTAName, BoroName) |>
    summarize(
        max_floors    = max(numfloors),
        median_floors = median(numfloors),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    slice_max(max_floors, n = 10)

q8 |>
    select(-NTA2020) |>
    gt() |>
    cols_label(NTAName = "Neighborhood", BoroName = "Borough",
               max_floors = "Tallest Building (floors)",
               median_floors = "Typical Building (median floors)") |>
    fmt_number(c(max_floors, median_floors), decimals = 0) |>
    tab_header(title = "NYC Neighborhoods with the Tallest Buildings")
```

### Q9. Population Density Across NYC

```{r}
#| label: fig-q9-density-map
tract_density <- nyc_tracts |>
    mutate(
        area_sqmi = as.numeric(units::set_units(st_area(geometry), "mi^2")),
        density   = if_else(totalE > 0, totalE / area_sqmi, NA_real_)
    )

ggplot(tract_density) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = density), color = NA) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", labels = comma,
                         na.value = "grey85", name = "People per\nsq mile") +
    labs(title = "Population Density by Census Tract",
         subtitle = "ACS 2024 5-year; grey = no residents (parks, airports)") +
    theme_void()
```

### Q10. New Yorkers in Primarily Commercial Areas

```{r}
#| label: q10-commercial
# My definition (you decide!): a tract is "primarily commercial" if at least
# half of its building floor area is commercial (PLUTO comarea / bldgarea).
COMMERCIAL_CUTOFF <- 0.5

q10 <- tract_full |>
    filter(bldg_area > 0) |>
    mutate(com_share = com_area / bldg_area,
           primarily_commercial = com_share >= COMMERCIAL_CUTOFF)

commercial_tracts <- sum(q10$primarily_commercial)
commercial_pop    <- sum(q10$pop[q10$primarily_commercial], na.rm = TRUE)
commercial_pct    <- commercial_pop / sum(q10$pop, na.rm = TRUE)
```

## Beyond Ancestry: Birthplace and Income

```{r}
#| label: ec2-nepal-born
# Extra Credit #2a: how many people were born in Nepal (table B05006)?
# The Nepal line number in B05006 changes between years, so find it by
# its label instead of hardcoding it. Stops with an error if not found.
NEPAL_BORN_VAR <- acs1_vars |>
    filter(str_starts(name, "B05006_"), str_detect(label, "!!Nepal$")) |>
    pull(name)
stopifnot(length(NEPAL_BORN_VAR) == 1)

nepal_born_cbsa <- get_acs_cached(
    "cbsa_nepal_born_acs5",
    geography = "cbsa",
    variables = c(nepal_born = NEPAL_BORN_VAR),
    year = ACS_YEAR, survey = "acs5", output = "wide"
)

nepal_born_us <- get_acs_cached(
    "us_nepal_born_acs5",
    geography = "us",
    variables = c(nepal_born = NEPAL_BORN_VAR),
    year = ACS_YEAR, survey = "acs5", output = "wide"
)

us_pct_born_nepal <- nepal_born_us$nepal_bornE / us_pop$nepaleseE

cbsa_pop |>
    filter(!is.na(nepaleseE)) |>
    slice_max(nepaleseE, n = 5) |>
    left_join(nepal_born_cbsa |> select(GEOID, nepal_bornE), by = "GEOID") |>
    mutate(pct_born_nepal = nepal_bornE / nepaleseE) |>
    select(NAME, nepaleseE, nepal_bornE, pct_born_nepal) |>
    gt() |>
    cols_label(NAME = "Metro Area", nepaleseE = "Nepalese (ancestry)",
               nepal_bornE = "Born in Nepal",
               pct_born_nepal = "Born in Nepal (% of Nepalese)") |>
    fmt_number(c(nepaleseE, nepal_bornE), decimals = 0) |>
    fmt_percent(pct_born_nepal, decimals = 0) |>
    tab_header(title = "How Many Nepalese Americans Are Immigrants?",
               subtitle = "ACS 2024 5-year. Approximate: the two tables count people differently.")
```

```{r}
#| label: ec2-income
# Extra Credit #2b: median household income (B19013_001) by NYC tract.
# Medians can't be added up, so compare the income of the tract the
# typical Nepalese New Yorker lives in vs. the typical New Yorker.
nyc_income <- get_acs_cached(
    "nyc_tracts_income_acs5",
    geography = "tract",
    state     = "NY",
    county    = NYC_COUNTIES,
    variables = c(med_income = "B19013_001"),
    year = ACS_YEAR, survey = "acs5", output = "wide"
)

income_compare <- tract_lookup |>
    left_join(nyc_income |> select(GEOID, med_incomeE), by = "GEOID") |>
    filter(!is.na(med_incomeE))

nepalese_tract_income <- weighted.mean(income_compare$med_incomeE, income_compare$nepalese)
all_tract_income      <- weighted.mean(income_compare$med_incomeE, income_compare$pop)

tibble(
    group  = c("Nepalese New Yorkers", "All New Yorkers"),
    income = c(nepalese_tract_income, all_tract_income)
) |>
    gt() |>
    cols_label(group = "", income = "Median Household Income of Home Tract") |>
    fmt_currency(income, decimals = 0) |>
    tab_header(title = "Neighborhood Income: Nepalese vs. All New Yorkers",
               subtitle = "Population-weighted average of tract medians, ACS 2024 5-year")
```

```{r}
nta_res <- nta_data |>
    filter(NTAType == 0) |>
    mutate(tooltip = paste0(NTAName, " (", BoroName, ")\n",
                            comma(nepalese), " Nepalese residents\n",
                            percent(nepalese_share, 0.1), " of neighborhood"))

nyc_map <- ggplot(nta_res) +
    geom_sf_interactive(aes(fill = nepalese_share, tooltip = tooltip,
                            data_id = NTA2020),
                        color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
    geom_sf(data = nta_data |> filter(NTAType != 0),
            fill = "grey90", color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", direction = -1,
                         labels = percent, name = "Nepalese\nshare") +
    theme_void()

top_ntas <- nta_res |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    slice_max(nepalese, n = 15)

nyc_bars <- ggplot(top_ntas,
                   aes(x = nepalese, y = fct_reorder(NTAName, nepalese))) +
    geom_col_interactive(aes(tooltip = tooltip, data_id = NTA2020),
                         fill = "#7a2048") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = comma) +
    labs(x = "Nepalese residents", y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9)

girafe(
    ggobj = (nyc_map | nyc_bars) +
        plot_layout(widths = c(1.3, 1)) +
        plot_annotation(
            title    = "Nepalese Residents by NYC Neighborhood",
            subtitle = "ACS 2024 5-year; hover to compare. Grey = parks, airports, cemeteries"
        ),
    width_svg = 10, height_svg = 5.5,
    options = list(
        opts_hover(css = "stroke:black;stroke-width:1.5px;"),
        opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.35;"),
        opts_tooltip(css = "background:white;color:black;padding:6px;border-radius:4px;font-size:12px;")
    )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-map-us-metros
# Metro shapes (cached) + state outlines, with Alaska/Hawaii moved under the map
cbsa_geo <- get_acs_cached(
    "cbsa_nepalese_acs5_geom",
    geography = "cbsa",
    variables = c(total = "B01003_001", nepalese = GROUP_VAR),
    year      = ACS_YEAR,
    survey    = "acs5",
    output    = "wide",
    geometry  = TRUE
) |>
    filter(!str_detect(NAME, ", PR"), !is.na(nepaleseE), nepaleseE > 0) |>
    tigris::shift_geometry() |>
    st_centroid()

us_states <- tigris::states(cb = TRUE, resolution = "20m", year = ACS_YEAR) |>
    filter(!STUSPS %in% c("PR", "VI", "GU", "MP", "AS")) |>
    tigris::shift_geometry()

cbsa_geo <- cbsa_geo |>
    arrange(desc(nepaleseE)) |>   # big bubbles drawn first, small ones on top
    mutate(tooltip = paste0(NAME, "\n", comma(nepaleseE),
                            " Nepalese residents (±", comma(nepaleseM), ")"))

us_map <- ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = us_states, fill = "grey95", color = "white") +
    geom_sf_interactive(data = cbsa_geo,
                        aes(size = nepaleseE, tooltip = tooltip, data_id = GEOID),
                        color = "#d1495b", alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 14, labels = comma, name = "Nepalese\nresidents") +
    labs(title = "Where Nepalese Americans Live",
         subtitle = "Metro areas, ACS 2024 5-year; hover a bubble for details") +
    theme_void()

girafe(
    ggobj = us_map,
    width_svg = 10, height_svg = 6,
    options = list(
        opts_hover(css = "fill:#7a2048;stroke:black;"),
        opts_tooltip(css = "background:white;color:black;padding:6px;border-radius:4px;font-size:12px;")
    )
)
```
